big_story.headline: RBI Eases CRR Rules to Unclog Cash
big_story.subhead: CENTRAL BANK CUTS DAILY CRR MAINTENANCE REQUIREMENT TO 90% FROM 99% TO EASE LIQUIDITY
paragraphs: The Reserve Bank of India has announced a key operational relaxation to support banking sector liquidity as financial conditions tighten across the system. Starting December 1, commercial banks in India will only need to maintain a minimum daily Cash Reserve Ratio of 90%, down from the previous requirement of 99%. This move grants lenders significantly more operational flexibility in managing their daily cash reserves without altering the overall fortnight requirement.

The decision comes at a crucial time when systemic liquidity in the Indian banking system has experienced notable tightness due to seasonal outflows and tax payments. By lowering the daily mandatory holding threshold, banks can better navigate unexpected short-term liquidity shocks and temporary cash deficits. Financial analysts note that this operational tweak prevents unnecessary spikes in short-term interbank money market rates during volatile sessions.

For commercial bank treasury desks, the enhanced operational leeway means they can deploy available cash more efficiently across overnight money market instruments. Industry observers will closely monitor how smoothly money markets adjust to the new 90% daily threshold starting next week. The central bank's intervention highlights its proactive approach to preserving monetary stability while keeping credit channels smooth for the domestic economy.
big_story.pullbox: By lowering daily CRR maintenance to 90%, the RBI provides vital flexibility for bank treasuries to manage liquidity squeezes without sacrificing financial prudence.

explains.title: What is Cash Reserve Ratio?
paragraphs: Cash Reserve Ratio, or CRR, is the specified percentage of total deposits that commercial banks are required to park with the central bank as cash reserves. Banks do not earn any interest income on these mandatory reserve balances maintained with the Reserve Bank of India.

While the total CRR requirement is calculated over a two-week fortnightly period, the daily maintenance rule sets the absolute minimum cash percentage banks must hold every single day. Reducing this daily requirement gives banks operational flexibility to handle temporary cash shortfalls without triggering regulatory penalties.

Indian semiconductor design startup C2i Semiconductors has raised $15 million in a fresh funding round led by venture capital firm Peak XV. Backed by the government's Design Linked Incentive scheme, this capital injection marks the largest funding round ever recorded for an Indian chip startup.

The successful fundraise highlights growing investor enthusiasm for domestic deep-tech and hardware innovation amid shifting global semiconductor supply chains. C2i Semiconductors plans to deploy the capital toward expanding its advanced engineering capabilities and accelerating product development for domestic chip designs.

story_1.headline: AirTrunk Commits ₹3 Lakh Crore to Digital Infra
paragraphs: Prime Minister Narendra Modi has welcomed global data center operator AirTrunk’s massive ₹3 lakh crore investment plan aimed at building digital infrastructure across India. The announcement highlights growing international confidence in India’s rapidly expanding cloud computing and digital ecosystem.
The planned capital deployment is expected to significantly boost server capacity and support the nation's accelerating demand for data storage and artificial intelligence capabilities.

story_2.headline: OpenAI Countersues Apple Over Trade Secrets
paragraphs: OpenAI has filed a countersuit against Apple, accusing the technology company of stealing trade secrets as competition in artificial intelligence accelerates. The legal battle marks a dramatic escalation between two prominent Silicon Valley players.
The dispute underscores rising tensions over proprietary technology and talent acquisition as tech giants compete for dominance in advanced AI development.

story_3.headline: RBI Sets Rules for Bank Debit Holds on Mule Accounts
paragraphs: The Reserve Bank of India has introduced new regulations allowing commercial banks to place debit holds on highly suspicious transactions linked to money mule accounts. The framework sets strict timelines and operational rules to combat cyber fraud and safeguard account holders.

geopolitics.headline: India and EU Hold 12th Foreign Policy and Security Talks
paragraphs: India and the European Union held the 12th round of their Foreign Policy and Security Consultations to address key international developments. Both delegations reaffirmed their joint commitment to Ukraine peace, Indo-Pacific stability, and counterterrorism initiatives. The dialogue highlights expanding strategic alignment between New Delhi and Brussels across foreign policy priorities.

Beyond diplomatic alignments, security in the Indo-Pacific remains crucial for safeguarding vital maritime shipping lanes connecting Indian commerce to European buyers. Balancing strategic autonomy on regional conflicts while bolstering trade links remains a central focus for Indian policymakers. Enhanced security cooperation is expected to build stability ahead of upcoming bilateral economic engagements.

big_story.headline: RBI Governor Pegs AI's MSME Economic Value at $685 Billion
big_story.text: The Reserve Bank of India Governor highlighted that artificial intelligence holds a potential economic value of $685 billion for India's micro, small, and medium enterprises. Urging small businesses to accelerate AI adoption, the central bank chief emphasized its role in driving efficiency and global competitiveness. For India, empowering MSMEs through technology is essential to achieve sustainable long-term economic growth.

big_story.headline: Siemens Energy India Crosses ₹10,000 Crore Revenue Milestone
big_story.text: Siemens Energy India announced that its annual revenue has surpassed the ₹10,000 crore milestone, reflecting robust demand across energy infrastructure sectors. The performance underscores expanding industrial activity and power equipment needs in the domestic market. This achievement highlights strong capital expenditure in India's energy transition and grid modernization drives.

venture_vault.headline: Bloom Hotels Secures ₹700 Crore Expansion Investment
venture_vault.text: Indian hospitality brand Bloom Hotels has raised ₹700 crore from private equity firm Kedaara Capital to fuel its expansion plans across key urban markets. The investment will support scaling its property footprint and strengthening operating capabilities. This significant capital influx reflects growing investor confidence in India's booming domestic travel and tourism sector.

venture_vault.headline: Fine Jewellery Brand GIVA Raises ₹90 Crore from BlackSoil
venture_vault.text: Direct-to-consumer jewellery startup GIVA has raised ₹90 crore in capital from BlackSoil to accelerate its offline retail expansion and market presence. The funding will enable the brand to open new physical stores and enhance supply chain infrastructure nationwide. The deal underscores strong momentum in India's consumer brand ecosystem as premium retail demand grows.

geopolitics.headline: India-EU Free Trade Pact Slated for Signing on 16 December
geopolitics.text: India and the European Union are set to sign their landmark Free Trade Agreement on 16 December during Prime Minister Narendra Modi's visit to Brussels. The historic pact is expected to enter into force by March-April 2027, unlocking market access and reducing tariffs. For India, this agreement promises deeper trade ties and enhanced market access for domestic exports to European markets.

geopolitics.headline: India-US Trade Deal Nearing Completion, Says Piyush Goyal
geopolitics.text: Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal announced that the long-anticipated India-US trade deal is nearing completion. The prospective agreement aims to ease tariff friction and boost bilateral commerce across key sectors. Finalizing this deal will strengthen strategic economic cooperation and deepen trade integration between the two partner nations.
